contracts: Cancel an actually registered withdrawing controller's course before native stops/notifications; ignore stale private requests.
Publish replacement player NavData after withdrawal and before Auto registration.
Admit exact registered controller instances at normal/SFF manager dispatch; preserve same-instance region migration.
Return Finished only at the terminal LowFuelRetreat withdrawal; preserve nonterminal Failure and target-selection policy.

scope: Every direct native AIShipManager.UnregisterShip call. Dispositions distinguish source review from executed callers. New assembly bytes invalidate this review, even if call counts match.

callers.note: Body-object branch retires registration and hides; other branch destroys hull after regional crew policy. No replacement course is assigned by this method. Player-connected preservation bypasses cleanup and migrates the same controller without UnregisterShip.
No living conscious eligible crew remains. Preserve crew readiness policy; native stops already apply. Docked police boarding exception is implemented separately.
Ship overload resolves current registry object and forwards. No registered controller means no withdrawal. Do not turn this call into a blanket stop of manual or pre-registration navigation.
Wrong/absent local police crew causes retirement or hidden hull destruction. Patrol retargeting is a different branch that does not unregister.
Null/destroyed actor cleanup. Dispatch uses detached references: exact current registry identity is required, including before processing a stale destroyed entry.

Native crew/drop-off policy executes before hiding hull and recording retirement station. Retired course is not handed to a station controller. Audit fixture executes empty-crew case; it does not simulate crew transfer or destruction.

Removes world/projectile membership then retires AI and destroys components. DestroyAndReload snapshots JSON before Destroy and constructs a new hull/controller afterward; snapshot course must survive.
Enable creates new Auto with HoldStationAutoPilot after withdrawal; reference stored separately. Disable/invalid target removes that mode. Old plotted course is not an input to station keeping.
Creates new HoldThrustAutoPilot after withdrawal, or disables it. Mode uses saved/GUI throttle; it does not inherit a plotted course.
Destroyed hulls are unregistered before dictionary removal. No replacement navigation in this branch.
Nav-station destruction unregisters, resets course, then applies Drift spin. Preserve damage and spin. Other equipment damage resets are independent, not permission for a universal reset hook.
Developer equivalent of nav destruction; no proof of ordinary gameplay reachability.
Timer expiry unregisters then returns Finished. No course handoff.
Less than one fuel unit unregisters and fails. Existing momentum remains; missile targeting and armed state are separate.
Base FlyTo failure and more than eight rejected paths unregister before optional stale cleanup. Successful stopping-distance arrival is a separate reset-only path.
DeltaVRemainingRCS <= 0 unregisters and fails. Dock links and hauling policy remain native; no group-wide cancellation is added.

Less than one RCS unit unregisters and returns Failure. Both combat consumers then resume firing/steering in that same invocation. Correct only this terminal return to Finished; preserve ordinary no-retreat Failure, target selection, Ceres policy and normal retreat progress.
No living regional-pirate crew satisfies boarding continuation. Terminal Finished return; no new route. Preserve authored pirate/surrender/subdued rules.
Authored command trees use terminal removal, including Auto completion. No replacement course is installed by this leaf.
Role policy either unregisters with optional cleanup or sends station distress then unregisters. Player proximity branch keeps Scav alive; preserve existing Scav recovery patches and asset policy.

Failure stops drives and clears plan before optional retirement. StickySequence can advance afterward, but actual native FlyTo/Dock reject the missing target without steering. Experimental status rewrite is unnecessary and excluded. Successful DTO plan installation must survive.
Native failed-target distress can unregister; ScavHelpLifecyclePatch retains the Scav controller instead. Cancellation must not invent a removal where the existing patch deliberately keeps authority.

1.1 adds an RCS delivery/capability-loss abort before the existing reactor safety abort. Both reset the plan/target before conditionally unregistering FlyToAutoPilot. Tests/AiPlannerDiagnosis/NativeRcsCompatibility.cs executes intact/damaged RCS playback with and without an exact registered Auto controller and the production completion/withdrawal patches. Ordinary successful completion remains a separate return boundary.
Player disables engagement: reset target/plan then conditionally unregister FlyToAutoPilot. No replacement course expected.
Only direct removal caller found publishing its replacement course before withdrawal. New publication must move after old withdrawal and before native replacement registration.
Developer test explicitly takes controller ownership; not ordinary gameplay policy.
Coroutine test withdraws before test setup; no shipping AI handoff is inferred.
